name: Marketing agency hero: large centered headline permanently clipped to an inverted-color window of a city-lights photo, shifting as the page scrolls
notes: Every line of the headline is masked now — no plain fallback line. Each h1 span sets background-image to the same hero photo, background-clip:text, then filter:invert(1) saturate(1.3) contrast(1.3) brightness(1.2), so the letters read as a bright inverted-color 'window' cut into the dark photo behind them, permanently on. Runs on city-lights-night.jpg (a starry night skyline with saturated red/teal/blue reflections) because the color variety and inverted starfield read as literal texture through the letters; pick a similarly high-contrast, colorful night/light-source photo if swapping it out, not a flat daylight shot. background-size is auto 230% (not plain 'cover') with background-position center 62% — at most hero aspect ratios 'cover' shows this photo's full height with no vertical crop room, which parks the top headline line over the empty near-black sky (inverts to near-flat white, reading as if the mask were 'off'); zooming in and biasing toward 62% keeps every line over the busy skyline/reflection band instead, so the invert effect stays visibly on everywhere the heading sits. Both image layers are pinned to the viewport rather than scrolling with the page — .hero-bg is position:fixed and .mask-heading span uses background-attachment:fixed — so as the page scrolls, the pinned crop stays put while the headline (normal in-flow content) slides over it, and each letter reveals a different part of the same image as it moves past. Verified via getComputedStyle(...).position/backgroundAttachment staying 'fixed' at multiple scroll positions, and the visible crop behind the letters visibly changing as hero-main scrolls up over the still-pinned background. .hero-main is align-items:center + text-align:center and the heading's clamp() runs up to 11rem — deliberately large and centered. The old dark linear-gradient shadow over the photo (.hero::after) is gone entirely so the city itself reads bright and clear; non-masked text (eyebrow, dek, ghost button, foot stats) got text-shadow and/or a small blurred dark pill background instead, scoped to just that text. Both fixed layers fall back to normal scroll under 720px width and prefers-reduced-motion. A second '.scroll-demo' section (paper background, 3-column capability grid) is appended after the hero purely so this file has something to scroll into on its own — it's explicitly commented as library-only and should be deleted when pulling the hero into a real page, which otherwise supplies its own next section. Confirmed the pinned .hero-bg doesn't bleed through onto that later section (a real risk with position:fixed inside an isolation:isolate ancestor in some render paths) by scrolling past the hero in a fresh preview tab and checking the paper section renders opaque on top, not underneath the pinned photo.
